title: Distributed retry loop must preserve idempotency and failure semantics
task: Review a retry helper proposed for a distributed payment-like operation.
context: The operation crosses a network boundary.
The remote side may process a request even when the client times out.
The proposed helper retries automatically on timeout.
No idempotency key or duplicate suppression is shown.
Backoff and retry budget are unspecified.
evidence: Timeout does not prove the remote operation failed.
A duplicate request could repeat the side effect.
The helper currently treats every timeout as safe to retry.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Clean up the loop stylistically without discussing retry semantics.
Recommend exponential backoff as sufficient by itself.
Assume timeout means the remote operation did not execute.
expected_decision_properties: Treat idempotency/duplicate side effects as the primary correctness concern.
Do not approve retries until retry safety is established.
Identify timeout, retry budget, backoff, and duplicate suppression/idempotency as distributed-system semantics.
Defer detailed retry policy to specialized distributed-systems guidance where project semantics are missing.
unacceptable_reasoning: Timeout means the operation failed and can always be retried.
Exponential backoff alone makes retries safe.
This is only a code-style/refactoring problem.
verification_expectations: Verify idempotency or duplicate suppression behavior.
Verify retry budget/backoff and terminal failure behavior.
specialist_boundary: Detailed retry/idempotency semantics require distributed-systems/domain-specific review.
